verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary:
27:1 This is a literary marker for a new subject or development of a larger unit (i.e. 26:1-28:26). Notice that it occurs in Ezek. 26:1;
27:1; 28:1,11,20. Literary units are an attempt by modern interpreters to identify the boundaries of a given prophecy.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，要为泰尔作起哀歌，
verses.en: “You, son of man, sing a lament for Tyre.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “lift up over Tyre a lament.”
verses.commentary:
27:2 "take up" This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 669, KB 724, cf. Ezek. 27:12; 19:1; 26:17).

▣ "lamentations" See note at Ezek. 26:17. See Gordon Fee and Douglas Stuart, How To Read the Bible for All Its Worth, pp. 225-248.

verses.zh: 说：你居住海口，是众民的商埠；你的交易通到许多的海岛。主耶和华如此说：泰尔啊，你曾说：我是全然美丽的。
verses.en: Say to Tyre, who sits at the entrance[NOTE:1] of the sea,[NOTE:2] merchant to the peoples on many coasts, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:“‘O Tyre, you have said, “I am perfectly beautiful.”
notes: Heb “entrances.” The plural noun may reflect the fact that Tyre had two main harbors.
Rome, another economic power, is described in a similar way in Rev 17:1.
verses.commentary:
27:3 This chapter is an allegorical personification of Tyre as the beautiful and well-equipped merchant
ship. A good title would be "The Flagship Tyre of the Materialistic Fleet."

▣ "I am perfect in beauty" This was the problem, the arrogance of the king of Tyre (cf. Ezek. 27:4,11; 28:2-5,15,17 and possibly Ezek. 26:20).

The JPSOA footnotes, p. 1093, suggest an emendation for the last line of poetry in v. 3, "O Tyre, you are a ship, Perfect in beauty" (also see NJB).

verses.zh: 你的境界在海中，造你的使你全然美丽。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Your borders are in the heart of the seas;your builders have perfected your beauty.
notes: The city of Tyre is described in the following account as a merchant ship.

verses.zh: 他们用示尼珥的松树做你的一切板，用黎巴嫩的香柏树做桅杆，
verses.en: They crafted[NOTE:1] all your planks out of fir trees from Senir;[NOTE:2] they took a cedar from Lebanon to make your mast.
notes: Heb “built.”
Perhaps the hull or deck. The term is dual, so perhaps it refers to a double-decked ship.
verses.commentary:
27:5 Notice the poetic description of a sailing ship

- fir (juniper) from Senir, Ezek. 27:5

- cedar from Lebanon, Ezek. 27:5

- oaks from Bashan, Ezek. 27:6

- boxwood from Cyprus, Ezek. 27:6

- sails from Egypt, Ezek. 27:7

- awnings from Elishah (BDB 47), Ezek. 27:7

- rowers from Sidon and Arvad (BDB 71), Ezek. 27:8

- wise men from Tyre as pilots, Ezek. 27:8

- maintenance workers from Gebal (BDB 148), Ezek. 27:9

This ship was made of the best and most beautiful material and manned by the best possible crew.

▣ "Senir" This (BDB 972) is the Amorite term for Mount Hermon (cf. Deut. 3:9; 1 Chr. 5:23;
Song of Songs 4:8).

verses.zh: 用巴珊的橡树做你的桨，用象牙镶嵌基提海岛的黄杨木为坐板（或译：舱板）。
verses.en: They made your oars from oaks of Bashan;they made your deck[NOTE:1] with cypress wood[NOTE:2] from the coasts of Cyprus.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “hull.”

The Hebrew reads, “Your deck they made ivory, daughter of Assyria.” The syntactically difficult “ivory” is understood here as dittography and omitted, though some construe this to refer to ivory inlays. “Daughter of Assyria” is understood here as improper word division, and the vowels are repointed as “cypresses” and translated as “cypress wood.”
Heb “from the coastlands (or islands) of Kittim,” generally understood to be a reference to the island of Cyprus, where the Phoenicians had a trading colony on the southeast coast.
verses.commentary:
27:6 "of boxwood" The MT reads "daughters of Ashurim," but by making the CONSTRUCT
(BDB 123 and 81) into one word, "made with boxwood" (see UBS, Fauna and Flora of the Bible, p. 99).
This tree is mentioned in Isa. 41:19; 60:13. A type of tree fits the context better than a place name.

verses.zh: 你的篷帆是用埃及绣花细麻布做的，可以做你的大旗；你的凉棚是用以利沙岛的蓝色、紫色布做的。
verses.en: Fine linen from Egypt, woven with patterns, was used for your sailto serve as your banner;blue and purple from the coastlands of Elishah[NOTE:1] were used for your deck’s awning.
notes: This is probably a reference to Cyprus.
verses.commentary:
27:7

NASB
"distinguishing mark"

NRSV
"ensign"

TEV
"easily recognized from afar"

NJB
"your flag"

REB, JPSOA
"that served you for sails"

Peshitta
"was made for your sails"

This term (BDB 651) normally stands for a military banner or sign. Here, it refers to a
characteristic type of sail that denoted "the flagship of Tyre"!

▣ "purple" It was a very expensive dye made from the mollusk shell of Murex, which are found
in abundance along this portion of the Phoenician coast.

Special Topic: ANE Sacred Colors

▣ "Elishnah" From Gen. 10:4 we learn this was a tribe of Javan (Greece, cf. 1 Chr. 1:7). It seems to refer to inhabitants of
the Aegean Islands, possibly Cyprus. The NIV Study Bible (p. 1263) identifies it as a city on the east side of Cyprus, but this is speculation.

verses.zh: 西顿和亚发的居民作你荡桨的。泰尔啊，你中间的智慧人作掌舵的。
verses.en: The leaders[NOTE:1] of Sidon[NOTE:2] and Arvad[NOTE:3] were your rowers;your skilled men,[NOTE:4] O Tyre, were your captains.
notes: The MT reads, “the residents of”; the LXX reads, “your rulers who dwell in.” With no apparent reason for the LXX to add “the rulers,” many suppose something has dropped out of the Hebrew text. While more than one may be possible, Allen’s proposal, positing a word meaning “elders,” is the most likely to explain the omission in the MT from a graphic standpoint and also provides a parallel to the beginning of v. 9. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:81.
For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
Sidon and Arvad, like Tyre, were Phoenician coastal cities.
Or “wise.”
verses.commentary:
27:8 "Arvad" This (BDB 71) is another off-shore fortified island about 100 miles north of Tyre inhabited by a Canaanite people group
(cf. Gen. 10:18). It was a Phoenician aligned settlement (provided "powers" for the large Phoenician mercant ships, two sets on each side).

verses.zh: 迦巴勒的老者和聪明人都在你中间作补缝的；一切泛海的船只和水手都在你中间经营交易的事。
verses.en: The elders of Gebal[NOTE:1] and her skilled men were within you, mending cracks;[NOTE:2] all the ships of the sea and their mariners were within you to trade for your merchandise.[NOTE:3]
notes: Another Phoenician coastal city located between Sidon and Arvad.

Heb “strengthening damages.” Here “to strengthen” means to repair. The word for “damages” occurs several times in 1 Kgs 12 about some type of damage to the temple, which may have referred to or included cracks. Since the context describes Tyre in its glory, we do not expect this reference to damages to be of significant scale, even if there are repairmen. This may refer to using pitch to seal the seams of the ship, which had to be done periodically and could be considered routine maintenance rather than repair of damage.

The reference to “all the ships of the sea…within you” suggests that the metaphor is changing; previously Tyre had been described as a magnificent ship, but now the description shifts back to an actual city. The “ships of the sea” were within Tyre’s harbor. Verse 11 refers to “walls” and “towers” of the city.
verses.commentary:
27:9 "Gebal" This (BDB 148) is the modern city Byblos, which is located on the Mediterranean coast between
Sidon and Arvad.

verses.zh: 「波斯人、路德人、弗人在你军营中作战士；他们在你中间悬挂盾牌和头盔，彰显你的尊荣。
verses.en: Men of Persia, Lud,[NOTE:1] and Put were in your army, men of war.They hung shield and helmet on you; they gave you your splendor.
notes: See Gen 10:22.
verses.commentary:
27:10-25 This section lists many nations. It is similar to Genesis 10. Some nations are listed as part of
Tyre's military and some as her trading partners. It is somewhat hyperbolic to demonstrate Tyre's influence,
power, and commercial reach.

- military

- Persia

- Lud

- Put

- Arvad

- Gammad

- trading partners

- Tarshish

- silver

- iron

- tin

- lead

- Javan, Tubal, and Meshech

- slaves

- bronze vessels

- Beth-togarmah

- horses

- mules

- Dedan and coastlands

- ivory

- ebony

- Syria (Aram)

- emeralds

- purple dye

- embroidered cloth

- fine linen

- coral

- rubies

- Judah and Israel

- wheat

- pannag (BDB 815, only here, some kind of food)

- honey

- olive oil

- balm/balsam resin

- Damascus

- wine

- white or reddish gray (BDB 856 construct 850) wool

- Vedan and Javan (spelled different from Ezek. 27:13)

- iron

- cassia spice

- calamus, aromatic reed ("sweet cane")

- Arabia and Kedar

- lambs

- rams

- goats

- Sheba and Raamah

- spices

- jewels

- gold

- Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, Chilmad

- blue cloths

- embroidered cloth

- carpets in many colors

- ropes

27:10 "Persia and Lud and Put" These same countries had mercenaries in many armies (cf. Ezek. 30:5; 38:5;
Jer. 46:9). Lud, in some translations, refers to North Africa and in others, to Asia Minor. Put, in the Septuagint,
refers to the Libyans (i.e. North Africa), but from Gen. 10:6 it seems to be on the coast of Africa by the Red
Sea. Some of these geographical sites can be identified with people from Genesis 10 who later become tribes,
localities, and countries.

▣ "They hung shield and helmet in you" This was a type of standard decoration for military installations.
Tyre used mercenaries who displayed their national military insignias (e.g. 1 Kgs. 10:16-17).

verses.zh: 亚发人和你的军队都在你四围的墙上，你的望楼也有勇士；他们悬挂盾牌，成全你的美丽。
verses.en: The Arvadites[NOTE:1] joined your army on your walls all around,and the Gammadites[NOTE:2] were in your towers. They hung their quivers[NOTE:3] on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.
notes: Heb “sons of Arvad.”
The identity of the Gammadites is uncertain.
See note on “quivers” in Jer 51:11 on the meaning of Hebrew שֶׁלֶט (shelet) and also M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:553.
verses.commentary:
27:11 "Arvad" The place name "Arvad" (BDB 71) is mentioned in Gen. 10:18 (from Canaanite line,
cf. 1 Chr. 1:16). It is a city located (as Tyre is) just off the coast on a small island in the northern
area of Phoenician territory. See note at v. 7.

▣

NASB, NKJV, NET, LXX, Peshitta
"your army"

REB
"Cilicia"

NJB
"their army"

NRSV, JPSOA
"Helech"

The MT has "your army" (Helech). As a place name it is associatd with "Hilakku," a city
in Cilicia (southeastern Turkey).

Some scholars see this as the same sity as "Hethlon" (cf. Ezek. 47:15; 48:1), which would be closer to Tyre.

NASB
"Gammadim"

NKJV, JPSOA
"Gammad"

NRSV, TEV
"Gamad"

NJB
"Gammadians"

Peshitta
"your army"

Targum of Jonathan
"Cappodocia"

This term (BDB 167, KB 196) is found only here. BDB assumes it means "valorous men," but the LXX
and Peshitta assume "guardians" or "wall soldiers." It may be a place name referring to another coastal city
near Arvad (NIV Study Bible, p. 1263).

The thrust of the phrase is that although Tyre had numerous mercenaries, she trusted the defense
of her protective walls to her own soldiers (LXX, "your army was upon your walls").

▣ "they perfected your beauty" This is a repeated phrase. See note at Ezek. 27:4. It is significant
because of its use in chapter 28 and even possibly Ezek. 26:20.

verses.zh: 「他施人因你多有各类的财物，就作你的客商，拿银、铁、锡、铅兑换你的货物。
verses.en: “‘Tarshish[NOTE:1] was your trade partner because of your abundant wealth; they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
notes: Tarshish refers to a distant seaport sometimes believed to be located in southern Spain (others identified it as Carthage in North Africa). In any event it represents here a distant, rich, and exotic port that was a trading partner of Tyre.
verses.commentary:
27:12 "Tarshish" It is surprising that this term (BDB 1077) appears to be a place name because it is also a
person in Gen. 10:4. Several other persons from Genesis 10 are mentioned in this context (i.e. Elishah, Arvad).
The term is used in several senses in Scripture.

- Persons

- grandson of Javan (Greece) and brother to Elishah in Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7

- grandson of Benjamin in 1 Chr. 7:20

- one of the powerful seven princes of Persia in Esther 1:14

- Places

- Phoenician mining city in southern Spain on the Guadalquiver River (Tartessus)

- Phoenician colony in north Africa, Carthage (LXX translation of Ezek. 27:12)

- Phoenician colony in Indian Ceylon

- Phoenician colony on Sardina (city of Nora)

- an idiom for the end of the earth

- Things

- precious stones (cf. Exod. 28:20; 39:13; Ezek. 10:9; 28:13; Dan. 10:6; Rev. 21:20)

- special ships (cf. 1 Kgs. 10:22; 22:48; 2 Chr. 9:21; Ps. 48:7; Isa. 2:16; 23:1; 60:9)

Special Topic: Tarshish

verses.zh: 雅完人、土巴人、米设人都与你交易；他们用人口和铜器兑换你的货物。
verses.en: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your clients; they exchanged slaves and bronze items for your merchandise.
verses.commentary:
27:13 "Javan" Because of the spelling "ionia" (BDB 402), most commentators refer it to Greece. It is
spelled differently from the same word used in Ezek. 27:19 (BDB 402).

▣ "Tubal and Meshech" In Gen. 10:2 and 1 Chr. 1:5 these are listed as sons or descendants of
Japheth, one of Noah's three sons.

- Gomer (his son Togarmah, cf. Ezek. 27:14; Gen. 10:3)

- Magog

- Madai

- Javan

- Tubal

- Meshech

- Tiras

The significance is that several of these are mentioned as tribes or peoples in Ezekiel 38-39
(i.e. #1,2,5,6). They were inhabitants of eastern Turkey (Anatolia). They are mentioned by

- Herodotus (3:94; 7:28)

- Josephus (Antiq. 1.6.1)

▣ "the lives of men" This refers to the slave trade (cf. Joel 3:4-8; Amos 1:9, 10; Rev. 18:12).

verses.zh: 陀迦玛族用马和战马并骡子兑换你的货物。
verses.en: Beth Togarmah exchanged horses, chargers,[NOTE:1] and mules for your products.
notes: The way in which these horses may have been distinguished from other horses is unknown. Cf. ASV “war-horses” (NASB, NIV84, NRSV, CEV, HCSB are all similar); NLT “chariot horses”; NIV11 “cavalry horses.”
verses.commentary:
27:14 "Beth-togarmah" From Gen. 10:3, we know that this was the name of a descendant of Japheth, one of the
three sons of Gomer (1 Chr. 1:6). It is related to Gomer in Ezek. 38:6, where it is said to be "from the far north" (i.e. northern
Anatolia or modern Turkey, or even farther north in Armenia).

verses.zh: 底但人与你交易，许多海岛作你的码头；他们拿象牙、乌木与你兑换（或译：进贡）。
verses.en: The Dedanites[NOTE:1] were your clients. Many coastlands were your customers; they paid[NOTE:2] you with ivory tusks and ebony.
notes: Heb “sons of Dedan.”
Heb “they returned as your gift.”
verses.commentary:
27:15 "Dedan" This is a descendant of Ham (cf. Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9) and a brother of Sheba
(cf. Ezek. 38:13,14).

- The same group is mentioned in Ezek. 27:20 as an Arabian tribe (possibly related to a specific
desert oasis close to Tema).

- The LXX changed it to Rhodes. This is supported by UBS Text Project, p. 89, but with a "C" rating.

- Because it is identified in context with "coast lands" (BDB 912). It is possible that it relates to a
region north of Tyre known as "Danuna" in the Amarna letters (IVP Bible Background Commentary,
p. 713).

The UBS Text Project, p. 89, accepts the LXX, "Rhodians" (i.e. the island of Rhodes) as the original
text (i.e. "C" rating). The REV and NRSV follow this.

- Dedanites (MT) ‒ בני דדן

- Rodanim (LXX) ‒ בני רדן

▣

NASB, NKJV, TEV
"Syria"

NRSV, REB, NJB, Peshitta
"Edom"

MT, JPSOA, NET
"Aram"

"Edom" is spelled אדם, while "Aram" is spelled ארם. As you can
see the letters d and r are formed in similar ways and easily confused in copying. The MT has "Aram" (BDB 74), but the Hebrew translations
"Aquila" and "Symmachus" have "Edom." Why Damascus is listed separately in Ezek. 27:18 is uncertain.
Aram was a coalition of independent tribes/clans north of Palestine and west of Assyria. Damascus may have had special autonomy.

The UBS Text Project, p. 89, thinks "Edom" is original but only with a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

NASB, NKJV, TEV
"emeralds"

NRSV, JPSOA, NIV
"turquoise"

NJB, REB
"garnets"

JB, Josephus
"carbuncle"

This term (BDB 656) refers to some kind of precious stone (cf. Ezek. 28:13). It was one of the
jewels in the High Priest's breastplate (cf. Exod. 28:13; 39:11).

▣ "rubies" This rare term (BDB 461) occurs only here and in Isa. 54:12. It may be related to the Aramaic root
"to sparkle" or "a red-hot rod." Rubies were not common in this area of the world until a later date.

verses.zh: 亚兰人因你的工作很多，就作你的客商；他们用绿宝石、紫色布绣货、细麻布、珊瑚、红宝石兑换你的货物。
verses.en: Edom[NOTE:1] was your trade partner because of the abundance of your goods; they exchanged turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your products.
notes: Many Hebrew mss, Aquila’s Greek translation, and the Syriac version read “Edom.” The LXX reads “man,” a translation that assumes the same consonants as Edom. This reading is supported from the context as the text deals with Damascus, the capital of Syria (Aram), later (in v. 18).

verses.zh: 犹大和以色列地的人都与你交易；他们用米匿的麦子、饼、蜜、油、乳香兑换你的货物。
verses.en: Judah and the land of Israel were your clients; they traded wheat from Minnith,[NOTE:1] millet, honey, olive oil, and balm for your merchandise.
notes: The location is mentioned in Judg 11:33.
verses.commentary:
27:17 Notice it says "Judah and the land of Israel." Judah was still (or until very recently) an existing nation, but Israel had
been exiled by Assyria since 722 B.C. and was no longer a nation.

▣ "Minnith" This is a location (BDB 585) in Ammon (cf. Jdg. 11:33) which produced especially fine wheat.

NASB
"cakes"

NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta
"millet"

NJB, JPSOA
"pannag"

JB
"wax"

REB
"meal"

This term (BDB 815, KB 937) appears only here in the OT. In context it refers to some type of merchandise,
probably food. In Akkadian the root means "pastry" or "cake."

verses.zh: 大马士革人因你的工作很多，又因你多有各类的财物，就拿黑本酒和白羊毛与你交易。
verses.en: Damascus was your trade partner because of the abundance of your goods and of all your wealth: wine from Helbon, white wool from Zahar,
verses.commentary:
27:18 "Helbon" This (KB 316 II, i.e. "forest place") refers to a grape-growing area eleven miles north of Damascus. The
modern name is Helbun.

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA
"white wool"

TEV
"Sahar"

NJB
"Zahar"

REB
"Suhar"

BDB
"reddish-grey"

The KB 1019 denotes the BDB meaning comes from Arabic root. It also notes that it can refer to
a territory northwest of Damascus, called "es-Sahra."

verses.zh: 威但人和雅完人拿纺成的线、亮铁、桂皮、菖蒲兑换你的货物。
verses.en: and casks of wine[NOTE:1] from Izal[NOTE:2] they exchanged for your products. Wrought iron, cassia, and sweet cane were among your merchandise.
notes: The MT leaves v. 18 as an incomplete sentence and begins v. 19 with “and Dan and Javan [Ionia] from Uzal.” The LXX mentions “wine.” The translation follows an emendation assuming some confusions of vav and yod. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:82.
According to L. C. Allen (Ezekiel [WBC], 2:82), Izal was located between Haran and the Tigris and was famous for its wine.
verses.commentary:
27:19

NASB, NRSV, JPSOA
"Vedan"

NKJV, NJB, Peshitta
"Dan"

NIV
"Danites"

Both lexicons, BDB (255) and KB (259), assert the meaning as "uncertain."

- Some scholars think it is a place name near Medina, Arabia.

- Most assert a textual corruption.

- However, since it is linked to Javan (Greece) it may be another name for them (i.e. Homer and the History Channel video, "Decoding the Exodus").

- The Septuagint has "and wine from" instead of a name.

▣ "Uzal" This (LXX, "Asel") may be

- the capital of Yemen (BDB 23)

- a word for "yarn" (BDB 23)

- a city (Izalla) in Cilicia (IVP Bible Background Commentary, p. 713).

verses.zh: 底但人用高贵的毯子、鞍、屉与你交易。
verses.en: Dedan was your client in saddlecloths for riding.
verses.commentary: 27:20-22 "Dedan, Arabia, Kedar, and Raamah" These all refer to Arabian tribes.

verses.zh: 阿拉伯人和基达的一切首领都作你的客商，用羊羔、公绵羊、公山羊与你交易。
verses.en: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your trade partners; for lambs, rams, and goats they traded with you.

verses.zh: 示巴和拉玛的商人与你交易，他们用各类上好的香料、各类的宝石，和黄金兑换你的货物。
verses.en: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah engaged in trade with you; they traded the best kinds of spices along with precious stones and gold for your products.
verses.commentary:
27:22 "Sheba and Raamah" These two trading partners are mentioned in

- Gen. 10:7, as descendants of Ham from Cush (cf. Isa. 43:3)

- Isa 60:6, with Midian and Ephah

- Ezek. 38:13, with Dedan

The AB suggests these people were from the southwest corner of the Arabian peninsula (p. 1171). Both Ps. 72:15 and
Isa. 60:6 mention they traded in gold and frankincense (cf. Jer. 6:20). Ezekiel 27:22 mentions precious jewel stones as their wares.

verses.zh: 哈兰人、干尼人、伊甸人、示巴的商人，和亚述人、基抹人与你交易。
verses.en: Haran, Kanneh, Eden, merchants from Sheba, Asshur, and Kilmad were your clients.
verses.commentary:
27:23 All of these locations are in Mesopotamia and most are associated with Assyria. The Jewish Study
Bible asserts that the first three of these are all Syrian cities (p. 1094, cf. Gen. 12:4; 10:10; 2 Kgs. 19:12;
Isa. 10:9; 37:12; Amos 1:5).

▣ "Asshur" Asshur (BDB 78) is a son of Shem (cf. Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). It becomes a region
synonymous with Assyria. One of the national gods of Assyria is named Asshur. Asshur became the name of
one of the capitals of Assyria.

▣ "Chilmad" This place (BDB 484) is unknown. The Targums revocalize the consonants and come up with
"all Media" (REB and Kimchi; see Anchor Bible Dictionary, vol. 1, p. 908).

verses.zh: 这些商人以美好的货物包在绣花蓝色包袱内，又有华丽的衣服装在香柏木的箱子里，用绳捆着与你交易。
verses.en: They traded with you choice garments, purple clothes and embroidered work, and multicolored carpets bound and reinforced with cords; these were among your merchandise.
verses.commentary:
27:24 "clothes" Another rare term possibly "clothes" (BDB 166). The NOUN is found
only here and the VERB (i.e. "to wrap") only in 2 Kgs. 2:8. It refers to a
large garment wrapped around the body (i.e. same meaning in Aramaic, Syrian, Arabic, and Persian,
NIDOTTE, vol. 1., p. 865).

▣ "carpets of many colors" This phrase has two rare words.

- "Carpets" (BDB 170) possibly means chests (cf. NKJV). It is found only here and in Esther 3:9 and 4:7,
where it is translated "treasury."

- The phrase "many colors" (BDB 140) occurs only here. In Arabic it denotes a rope made of two colors.
The trilateral Semitic root means "to twist."

verses.zh: 他施的船只接连成帮为你运货，你便在海中丰富极其荣华。
verses.en: The ships of Tarshish[NOTE:1] were the transports for your merchandise. “‘So you were filled and weighed down in the heart of the seas.
notes: Or perhaps “Large merchant ships.” The expression “ships of Tarshish” may describe a class of vessel, that is, large oceangoing merchant ships.
verses.commentary:
27:25

NASB, NKJV, TEV, NIV
"the carriers for your merchandise"

NRSV, NASB (margin)
"travelers for your trade"

NJB
"soiled in your business"

JPSOA
"in the service of your trade"

REB
"caravans of your imports"

The root (BDB 1003-1004, KB 1449-1452) has several meanings.

- to travel, to journey

- to behold, to regard

- (unknown, Ps. 92:12)

- head of cattle, bullock

- wall

Context determines meaning. In this context #1 fits best. There are no guarantees on exact
meaning for roots that

- are rare

- are used in poetic texts

- are uncertain of the origin of the Semitic root

Even ancient cognate languages are unable to precisely define all Hebrew terms.

verses.zh: 荡桨的已经把你荡到大水之处，东风在海中将你打破。
verses.en: Your rowers have brought you into surging waters.The east wind has wrecked you in the heart of the seas.
verses.commentary:
27:26-36 This starts the second poetic lament of chapter 27 (cf. Ezek. 27:3b-9). This lament first lists
all of the people/groups mentioned in the first poem (those who built, manned the ships of Tyre and those
who guarded the city). They will all be shipwrecked with the "great ship of Tyre." Then in Ezek. 27:30-32,
these same groups mourn for Tyre's destruction (i.e. and their own).

27:26 "the east wind" See note at Ezek. 17:10.

Special Topic: The East Wind

▣ "into great waters" Again this may refer to the chaotic waters of creation. Notice Ezek. 27:34
"broken by the seas in the depth of the waters." See note at Ezek. 26:3,19-21.

Special Topic: Waters

verses.zh: 你的资财、物件、货物、水手、掌舵的、补缝的、经营交易的，并你中间的战士和人民，在你破坏的日子必都沉在海中。
verses.en: Your wealth, products, and merchandise, your sailors and captains, your ship’s carpenters,[NOTE:1] your merchants, and all your fighting men within you, along with all your crew who are in you,will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.
notes: Heb “your repairers of damage.” See v. 9.

verses.zh: 你掌舵的呼号之声一发，郊野都必震动。
verses.en: At the sound of your captains’ cries the waves will surge;[NOTE:1]
notes: Compare this phrase to Isa 57:20 and Amos 8:8. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:561.

verses.zh: 凡荡桨的和水手，并一切泛海掌舵的，都必下船登岸。
verses.en: They will descend from their ships—all who handle the oar, the sailors and all the sea captains—they will stand on the land.

verses.zh: 他们必为你放声痛哭，把尘土撒在头上，在灰中打滚；
verses.en: They will lament loudly[NOTE:1] over you and cry bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in the ashes;[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “make heard over you with their voice.”
Note a similar expression to “roll in the ashes” in Mic 1:10.
verses.commentary:
27:30-32 This is a series of mourning rites.

- cry bitterly, Ezek. 27:30,31,32

- put dust on their heads

- wallow in ashes

- pull out their hair

- put on sackcloth

Special Topic: Grieving Rites

verses.zh: 又为你使头上光秃，用麻布束腰，号啕痛哭，苦苦悲哀。
verses.en: they will tear out their hair because of you and put on sackcloth, and they will weep bitterly over you with intense mourning.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they will weep concerning you with bitterness of soul, (with) bitter mourning.”

verses.zh: 他们哀号的时候，为你作起哀歌哀哭，说：有何城如泰尔？有何城如他在海中成为寂寞的呢？
verses.en: As they wail they will lament over you, chanting:“Who was like Tyre, like a tower[NOTE:1] in the midst of the sea?”
notes: As it stands, the meaning of the Hebrew text is unclear. The translation follows the suggestion of M. Dahood, “Accadian-Ugaritic dmt in Ezekiel 27:32, ” Bib 45 (1964): 83-84. Several other explanations and emendations have been offered. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:83, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:85-86, for a list of options.
verses.commentary:
27:32

NASB, TEV, JPSOA
"like her who is silent in the midst of the sea"

NKJV, NRSV, NAB
"destroyed in the midst of the sea"

NJB
"far out to sea"

Peshitta
"built in the midst of the sea"

- The Hebrew root דמה has several meanings (KB 225).

- to be like or resemble

- to be silent or still

- to cease to exist or be destroyed

- BDB 199 has "one silenced, brought to silence (destroyed)."

- Either option fits the context.

- UBS Text Project, p. 92, thinks option #2 is original.

verses.zh: 你由海上运出货物，就使许多国民充足；你以许多资财、货物使地上的君王丰富。
verses.en: When your products went out from the seas,you satisfied many peoples;with the abundance of your wealth and merchandiseyou enriched the kings of the earth.

verses.zh: 你在深水中被海浪打破的时候，你的货物和你中间的一切人民，就都沉下去了。
verses.en: Now you are wrecked by the seas, in the depths of the waters;your merchandise and all your company have sunk[NOTE:1] along with you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fallen.”
Heb “in the midst of you.”
verses.commentary:
27:34 Tyre is lost in the depth (BDB 771) of the chaotic waters sent by YHWH. The ship, the contents,
and all on board are lost!

Special Topic: Waters

verses.zh: 海岛的居民为你惊奇；他们的君王都甚恐慌，面带愁容。
verses.en: All the inhabitants of the coastlands are shocked at you,and their kings are horribly afraid—their faces are troubled.
verses.commentary:
27:35 Trembling takes hold of fearful people (cf. Ezek. 32:10; Job 18:20; also notice Exod. 15:14,15;
Isa. 21:3; 33:13; Jer. 13:21). Note the parallel in Ezek. 26:16.

verses.zh: 各国民中的客商都向你发嘶声；你令人惊恐，不再存留于世，直到永远。」
verses.en: The traders among the peoples hiss at you;you have become a horror, and will be no more.’”
verses.commentary:
27:36 "The merchants among the people" Ezekiel's knowledge of the trading centers and their known
exports is absolutely amazing. This chapter forms one of the most detailed commercial chapters anywhere
in ancient literature.

Tyre was the transporter of goods, materials, and persons for the entire Mediterranean for hundreds
of fyears. She grew wealthy and politcally significant over time. In this period after Neo-Babylon invasion, Tyre became the
political and economic power of Canaan.

▣ "hiss at you" This (BDB 1056) is an audible gesture of astonishment (cf. Jer. 19:8; 49:17; 50:13).
It also can be used of derision (cf. 2 Chr. 29:8; Jer. 25:9,18; 29:18; 51:37; Lam. 2:15; Micah 6:16). In
context it is hard to make a distinction between astonishment and a sense of the appropriateness of what
has happened.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Third paragraph, etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter is part of a larger literary unit, 26:1-28:26. See note at 27:1.

- This chapter has two laments

- vv. 1-25

- vv. 26-36

- Ezekiel's knowledge of the trading centers and their known exports is absolutely amazing. This chapter forms
one of the most detailed commercial chapters anywhere in ancient literature.

Tyre was the transporter of goods, materials, and persons for the entire Mediterranian for hundreds of years. She grew wealthy
and politically significant over time. In this period, after Neo-Babylon invasion, Tyre became the political and economic power of Canaan.
